name: Password reset poisoning
description:
The application builds the password reset link from a request header the client controls: the Host header or a forwarding header such as X-Forwarded-Host. An attacker requests a reset for a victim with the header naming the attacker's own host; the victim receives a genuine reset message whose link points at the attacker, and clicking it hands the attacker the victim's token.

burpsy reports this only when a link to a random canary host it put in the header appears in the response or in the reset message mailed to the test identity.

This row is burpsy's own: Burp's issue catalogue has no password-reset rows.
remediation: Build absolute links from a configured, trusted base URL. Never derive them from the Host header or any X-Forwarded-*/Forwarded header, and have the front end overwrite forwarding headers rather than pass client-supplied ones through.

references.title: OWASP WSTG: Testing for Weak Password Change or Reset Functionalities (WSTG-ATHN-09)

vulnerabilityClassifications.title: CWE-640: Weak Password Recovery Mechanism for Forgotten Password
